linkedin.text:
🚨 You've been re-explaining the same architecture to your AI coding agent for the third time this week.

Why? Because agents lose everything when the session ends. Every switch from Claude Code to Codex means starting from zero. Every resume means re-stating your tech stack, your failed approaches, your open questions.

ai-memory fixes this.

✅ Persistent wiki compiled from lifecycle observations
✅ Cross-agent handoffs that preserve context
✅ Plain markdown in a git repo—grep it, back it up, open it in Obsidian

No vector database to manage. No manual note-taking ceremony. Just install the hooks and your agents start remembering.

Quit Claude Code mid-task. Start Codex hours later. Your next agent sees "where you left off" before the first prompt.

Over 3,500 stars. MIT licensed. Supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and 15+ other harnesses.

⭐ Search "akitaonrails ai-memory" on GitHub.

How much time do you lose re-explaining context to your agent every week?
